Name: Caesar Augustus
Summary: Caesar Augustus was the first Roman emperor. His decree that all the world be taxed sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born, fulfilling the prophecy of the Messiah's birthplace.
KeyStory: An emperor's census moved a carpenter's family to Bethlehem, and prophecy was fulfilled by a tax form.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
LifeLesson: God uses the decrees of empires to keep His promises. Augustus thought he was counting subjects; he was staging a birth.
